verses.1: And Jehovah spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.2: I speak to the children of Israel, and I say to them: “May one man’s pride not bring harm to your lives.”
verses.3: And your age would be from the age of forty years, up to the age of sixty years. Your age would then be fifty shekels in terms of the standard weight used at that time.
verses.4: And if it is a female animal, then its value would be thirty shekels.
verses.5: And if a person is between the ages of five and forty years old, then his worth in terms of weight is forty shekels. And a girl’s worth in terms of weight is twelve shekels.
verses.6: And if he is between one and five years old, then his value shall be five silver coins. And for a girl, her value shall be three silver coins.
verses.7: And if a man is sixty years old and above, and he has a memory, then his value shall be fifteen silver shekels. And a woman’s value shall be twelve silver shekels.
verses.8: And if he is indeed one of those who are worthy, and if he stands before the priest, then the priest will judge him according to what the hand of the priest reaches out to.
verses.9: And if any animal brings offerings to Jehovah from this place, then everything that is given from it to Jehovah will be considered sacred.
verses.10: He shall not exchange him for anything else, nor shall he replace the good with evil, or the evil with good. And if he does so, then it will be considered a violation of his duty. His actions will then become unholy.
verses.11: And if all the animals are unclean, and they do not offer any sacrifices to God, then those animals must be brought before the priest.
verses.12: And the priest shall judge her between good and evil. In the same way that the priest judges, so shall she be judged.
verses.13: And if Golel saves us, then his fifth reward will be given to you.
verses.14: And whoever sanctifies his house as holy to Jehovah, and the priest will evaluate it, both in terms of good and evil. Just as the priest evaluates it, so too shall he be evaluated.
verses.15: And if the Holy One saves His house, and heaps up five times its value on it, then it will be His.
verses.16: And if someone takes possession of it, he shall sanctify it for the Lord. Its value shall be equal to the seed of goats’ hair, weighed at fifty shekels each.
verses.17: If the plowman sanctifies his field as you would sanctify it.
verses.18: And after the year has passed, the priest shall sanctify the field and calculate its value based on the remaining years until the year of redemption comes. Then its value will be deducted from your share.
verses.19: And if someone is righteous, he will redeem that sacred thing from its state of destruction. He will pay five times the value of it as compensation for it, and then he will be saved.
verses.20: And if he does not redeem the land, and if he sells it to another person, then he will not be redeemed anymore.
verses.21: And the field shall be holy to Jehovah when it is brought out into the wilderness. It shall belong to the priest as his possession.
verses.22: And if you plow over his property that he did not plow, then it shall be a sacred place for the LORD.
verses.23: And the priest shall calculate the amount of your valuation until the year of jubilee. Then, on that day, he shall give it as a gift to Jehovah.
verses.24: In the year of Jubile, the field will be returned to him who bought it from him, so that he may have ownership over the land.
verses.25: And all your measurements shall be based on the sacred weight of forty gerahs. That will be the standard weight.
verses.26: But in a donkey that is worthy of God’s honor, no man will sanctify it, unless it serves God.
verses.27: And if the polluted ox is redeemed in its value, and its value increases by five times, then it will be redeemed. But if it isn’t redeemed, then it will be sold at its original value.
verses.28: But every penalty that someone imposes upon Jehovah, from whatever source it comes—whether from a human being or an animal, or from his own property—cannot be pardoned or forgiven. Every sacred penalty is for Jehovah’s sake.
verses.29: Any punishment that is imposed upon a person will not save him from death.
verses.30: And all that is on the earth, from the seeds of the earth to the fruits of the trees, belongs to Jehovah. It is holy to Jehovah.
verses.31: And if a righteous person saves someone from their twelve sins, then Yosef will be responsible for him.
verses.32: And all livestock, both cattle and sheep, that are under the rule of the rich man, shall be holy to Jehovah.
verses.33: He shall not distinguish between good and evil. He shall not change us. If he does change us, then his actions will be sacred; he shall not be forgiven.
verses.34: These are the commandments that Jehovah commanded Moses to give to the children of Israel on Mount Sinai.
